sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with Common Law influences in commercial and maritime sectors)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of April 27, 2015, as amended, on AML/CFT regulations; Law No. 129 of March 18, 2020, establishing the Unified Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales); Executive Decree No. 959 of July 9, 2021, implementing the RUBF; complemented by Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) binding guidelines and Public Registry client due diligence rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the founder's passport and dual identification document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport and ID civil registry authority of the founder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) issued within the last 90 days
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a Hague Convention signatory; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate founder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Registry or competent companies registrar in the founder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter and Foundation Statutes (Estatutos) duly executed and notarized in Panama or legalized if signed abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama or notary public in the foreign signatory jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization followed by Public Registry registration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, foundation guardians, protectors, beneficiaries and mandated signatories against the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) PEP and terrorist-financing lists, the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated list, and Panama's domestic criminal record registry. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, including establishment of source of wealth and source of funds, and preparation of a written risk assessment file in compliance with Law No. 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Reservation System (Aviso de Reserva de Nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be submitted in Spanish or transliterated into the Spanish alphabet. The name must be unique in the Public Registry and include the word 'Fundación'. Confusable names, surnames, abbreviations, and words suggesting a false link to public or regulated bodies are rejected. Foreign businesses must present a certified translation into Spanish before registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANCO / BANK / CREDITO – requires prior authorization of the Superintendency of Banks if banking activities are intended
SEGURO / REASEGURO – requires insurance and reinsurance regulator approval
GOBIERNO / MINISTERIO / NACIONAL – prohibited when falsely implying an official Panamanian state entity
MINERA / PETROLEO / HIDROCARBURO – subject to sector-specific concession authority approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be renewed for successive 30-day periods by filing a written renewal request before the Public Registry. Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (Recurso de Apelación) within five business days before the Directorate General of the Public Registry, attaching the rejection resolution, the proposed name, and evidence of non-conflicting registration in the public name database.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible as non-statutory management and sales addresses for an ISIC 6201 digital health app business, but the foundation must maintain a physical statutory registered office in Panama where the resident agent and corporate records are kept. A virtual office cannot replace the physical statutory address required by Panamanian law.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 5% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection in the first year for a low-risk digital health app company, increasing to a more likely 15–25% if the UAF flags unusual or high-risk transaction patterns.

Notarization and legal drafting of Foundation Charter and Statutes
Public Registry registration fee for the Private Interest Foundation
First-year resident agent and registered office service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent firm in Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing with the Unified Beneficial Owner Registry (RUBF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille / consular legalization of foreign documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Ministry of Foreign Affairs or foreign competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular tariff and courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of apostilled foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Peruvian? No, Panamanian translation market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), Articles 2, 5, 6, 8, 12, 18, 19 and 33; implementing Executive Decree No. 16 of 7 October 1999; subsidiarily, the Código de Comercio de la República de Panamá and the registration norms of the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Carta Fundacional (Foundation Charter), executed before a Notary of the Circuit as a public instrument (Escritura Pública) and inscribed in the Special Registry of Private Interest Foundations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 de 1995 imposes no statutory minimum; the Foundation must hold an initial endowment (patrimonio fundacional) adequate for its stated purpose, set at US$10,000 for this vehicle. No escrow or banker's deposit certificate is required; the endowment is contributed directly by the Founder and evidenced in the notarized Charter. The endowment may comprise cash, securities or software assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL. At a duly convened meeting held on the incorporation date, it was unanimously RESOLVED: (1) the initial endowment of US$10,000 tendered by the Founder is accepted and recorded as the Foundation's patrimony; (2) the registered office at the Resident Agent's address in Panama City is adopted as the statutory seat; (3) the Resident Agent is ratified with full authority before the Public Registry; (4) the designated persons are appointed to the Foundation Council with powers under the Foundation Regulations; (5) the Council is authorized to open bank accounts and execute agreements for the fitness application enterprise; and (6) the Resident Agent shall file all registration documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance, charter drafting and notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría del Circuito de Panamá) with pre-registration name search at the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a foundation name search (one primary and two alternative names) at the Public Registry. Instruct the Resident Agent to draft the Carta Fundacional (founder, endowment, Council members, beneficiaries, registered office) and the Reglamento de la Fundación per Law 25 de 1995. The Founder executes the instrument before the Notary; the Notary verifies identity and legality and elevates the instrument to an Escritura Pública.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of Founder and Foundation Council members
Draft Foundation Charter and Foundation Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit the alternative names; if the Notary objects to a clause, amend the text by addendum and re-execute the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Resident Agent files the notarized Escritura Pública together with the fee receipt. The Registry verifies the endowment, registered office, Resident Agent appointment and beneficiaries, then inscribes the Foundation in the Special Registry of Private Interest Foundations, granting legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Foundation Regulations (if any)
Certified identification of the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an observación (query), the Resident Agent files a written response within 3 business days; substantive defects are cured by a supplementary notarial act and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the First Foundation Council Resolution and book legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council of the Private Interest Foundation, with the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council and adopt the standard first resolution covering endowment acceptance, registered office, Council appointments and officer ratification. Record the minutes in the corporate book (Libro de Actas), then submit the corporate books for legalization (timbre and foliation) at the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Corporate books from an authorized printer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the minutes or the books, correct signatures, foliation or wording and re-submit within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer (RUC) registration and municipal Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; Dirección de Rentas, Municipality of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File DGI Form 010 to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) under Panama's territorial taxation regime. After the RUC is issued, file the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of Panama, pay the proportional municipal fee, and obtain the operating notice card for the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Registro of the Foundation
Certified copy of the Resident Agent license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the application, correct the taxpayer profile and re-file; municipal fee shortfalls are settled with surcharge within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data protection registration for biometric health telemetry data
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the health and fitness biometric data processing activity under Law 81 de 2019, submit the app privacy policy, record the data inventory and processing purposes, and designate a Data Protection Officer for special-category health data. Confirm that the non-clinical fitness tracker requires no medical-device sanitary registration.
required_dossiers: Appointment letter of the Data Protection Officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer ANTAI technical queries within 5 business days; rectify the data inventory and resubmit the registration without penalty if the query is answered timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of final certificate and legal standing confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalize the remaining corporate books (register of beneficiaries and endowment records), then request the certified certificate of registration (Certificado de Registro y Personería Jurídica) and certified copies of the inscribed Charter (fojas) for banking, app store and commercial counterparty onboarding.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney of the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains material errors, file a correction petition (reforma) before the Registry's Directorate General; correction is usually granted within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity is a digital software and telemetry service with no industrial factory or physical manufacturing component. Fiscal and municipal registrations (DGI RUC and Municipality of Panama Aviso de Operación) are the only operational clearances required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Notice); no sanitary registration (registro sanitario) or industrial operating permit applies to the non-clinical fitness tracking application.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de la República de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category I administrative/digital service activities are not enumerated under Executive Decree 123 de 2009 EIA categories; no environmental registration, full EIA report or prior environmental consultation is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC/stack emissions and no hazardous solid waste generation. Indirect compliance limited to secure disposal of electronic waste and adherence to Law 81 de 2019 biometric data protection standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá fire-safety inspection certificate for the registered office; structural load and occupancy inspection by the Dirección de Obras y Construcciones del Municipio de Panamá; workplace safety registration and medical clearance through the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) once employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; primary digital portal is SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Información Tributaria) at https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa, which consolidates RUC registration, taxpayer filings, electronic invoicing, and ITBMS declarations. Ancillary registries are the Registro Público de Panamá for the foundation charter and the relevant Municipio for the Aviso de Operación (business license).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) established under Law 25 of 1995: (1) Notarize and register the foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva) with the Registro Público, declaring the initial endowment, which is customarily and statutorily expected to be at least USD 10,000; (2) appoint the resident agent and the Foundation Council (Consejo de la Fundación) with the required Panamanian officers; (3) after registration, apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) for legal entities through the DGI SITIO portal, filing the corporate registration certificate and identifying the legal representative; (4) where the PIF engages in taxable business in Panama, also register as an ITBMS taxpayer and obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación; (5) a non-resident digital service provider without a Panamanian permanent establishment may obtain a simplified ITBMS registration via a Panamanian fiscal representative, which serves as the statutory TIN/VAT-ID for app-store collections.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US check-the-box election and no OECD hybrid-mismatch election exists in Panamanian law; the PIF is fixed by statute as a separate juridical person. Available elections include: (a) the simplified small-taxpayer regime for annual gross income up to B/. 36,000; (b) the standard ITBMS regime, including the exporter election to claim refunds of input ITBMS; (c) transitional elections under Law 52 of 2020 for entities migrating to the reformed income-tax code; and (d) charter elections on beneficiary designation and distribution structure, which determine the territorial-source treatment of distributions. Panama-source income of the PIF is taxed at the entity level; foreign-source income is outside the Panamanian tax net.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panamanian value-added tax applicable to goods, services, and digital services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (USD 36,000 equivalent at par) annual gross income for the simplified small-taxpayer fixed-quota regime; full ITBMS registration is mandatory from the first habitual taxable transfer in Panama, with no general de minimis exemption. Non-resident suppliers of digital services to consumers in Panama are subject to statutory ITBMS registration and collection duties. In-app sales through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing to Panamanian consumers are in-scope, while sales to non-resident users fall outside the ITBMS nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá) under DGI regulations, phased in by taxpayer category. VAT-registered businesses must issue invoices through the DGI-authorized platform or certified billing software using XML/API transmission, receiving a unique digital authorization code (stamp) in real time before issuance; each invoice must contain a QR code and the DGI tax identification of the issuer. Legacy fiscal printers remain temporarily permitted only for approved small taxpayers. Digital health-app operators in the standard ITBMS regime are on the mandatory electronic-issuance track, and input VAT credit or export refund claims generally require electronically authorized invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS is charged at 0% on (i) exports of tangible goods supported by an official Panamanian export declaration, and (ii) services rendered to non-resident customers that are wholly consumed or exploited outside Panama. For the health-fitness app tracker, zero-rating requires documentary proof that the end-user is non-resident (foreign billing address, non-Panamanian payment instrument, geolocation/IP data, and the license agreement) and that the digital service is consumed outside Panama. App-store commissions paid to Apple or Google are treated as imported services subject to reverse-charge ITBMS unless they support the PIF's own exported service; failure to substantiate the export converts the supply to a taxable 7% supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (Formulario Único de Exportación / DUE) for physical goods; for digital services, the export invoice, the license agreement, and the app-store transaction/delivery log
Bill of Lading or airway waybill for goods; for services, app-store payout statements and platform transaction records evidencing the foreign recipient
Inward remittance certificate (Comprobante de Ingreso de Divisas) or bank/Apple/Google payout evidence demonstrating receipt of foreign exchange proceeds
RUC and ITBMS registration certificate plus the foundation charter excerpt confirming the PIF as the exporting counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit export zero-rating claims within the statutory prescription period, which is generally five years and is suspended in cases of fraud or serious documentation defects. If export status is not substantiated, DGI assesses the 7% ITBMS on the gross supply, applies statutory default interest, and imposes fines up to 100% of the omitted tax depending on the degree of fault. Knowingly false export documentation constitutes tax fraud and may expose the PIF and its officers to criminal liability and to retrospective clawback of any refunded input ITBMS credits. The full documentation bundle, including FX remittance traceability and user-location evidence, must be retained for the entire prescription window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no central bank in the conventional sense; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking regulator, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent and treasury administrator for the State.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy; the U.S. dollar is legal tender and the Panamanian balboa exists only as a sub-unit coin at a fixed 1:1 exchange ratio. Both capital-account and current-account transactions are freely convertible and unrestricted in law. There are no exchange-control commissions, no central bank approval for foreign currency wires, and no hindrance to profit remittance. Dividends, distributions, and service fees may be repatriated freely, provided the bank obtains standard AML/KYC documentation and the relevant wire instruction is fully compliant with the Foreign Tax Information Exchange regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules in Panama. No timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or central-bank accounting requirement applies to export receipts. Export proceeds from the digital health-fitness app (Apple IAP/Google Play Billing settlements) may be retained in USD or any freely convertible currency and do not need to be converted into balboas or remitted to any Panamanian government authority.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business) are not licensed banks in Panama and do not provide membership of Panama's local clearing or automatic SBP regulatory recognition. They may onboard Panama-registered Private Interest Foundations only if the EMI's own licensing regime permits this jurisdiction, but they cannot serve as exclusive treasury rails for collection or settlement in Panama. Their use is legally permissible as a secondary liquidity corridor, but local banks are required for statutory account structure and for receiving final settlement of subscription receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The SBP-licensed banking practice materially requires physical KYC attendance for non-resident customers. For a Panama Private Interest Foundation, the founder, at least one council member, and all persons holding effective beneficial ownership must normally appear physically at the bank or before a Panamanian notary or a designated correspondent-notary/consul to complete signature verification and biometric checks. Remote onboarding is exceptionally available only for low-risk renewed relationships or with apostilled certified copies and a high-calibre professional introducer; however, most tier-one banks require a face-to-face interview for first-time PIF account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation perceived as a low-substance corporate vehicle with potential beneficial-owner concealment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated foundation charter (public deed) and registration certificate from the Public Registry of Panama; foundation council resolution appointing signatories; certified passports of all founding council members; AML/KYC questionnaire; signed declaration of sources of foundation assets; CRS/FATCA tax classification form; professional reference letter from the registered agent or an SBP-licensed asset manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency micro-transactions originating from Apple App Store and Google Play, creating the appearance of an unmonitored merchant aggregation flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal developer agreements with Apple and Google; app store merchant documentation; transaction monitoring and policy; evidence of end-user terms and conditions; geographic country-blocking rules; audited or internally prepared financial projections; IT/data-hosting contracts; AML program description; a business plan explaining subscriptions, refund protocols, and consent mechanisms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or council member appears to have multi-jurisdictional exposure or classified as a politically exposed person (PEP), triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full PEP status disclosure; independent source-of-wealth statement with bank statements, tax returns, and asset records; institutional portfolio and audit letters; notarized explanation of the business purpose; evidence of tax registration and good-standing in all relevant jurisdictions; SBP-required enhanced due diligence forms executed in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from a non-Panamanian jurisdiction with tax secrecy or sanctions-risk profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Origin of funds bank statement from the contributing entity; formal board/subscriber resolution; certified copies of agreements evidencing the underlying business purpose; legal opinion or notarized declaration confirming no tax fraud or money-laundering risk; country-specific tax identification certificates and CRS declaration; proof of economic substance and adequate professional registration of the app business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound initial and additional capital is routed by SWIFT MT103 wire from the founder's or subscriber's outside bank to the PIF's Panama bank account. The wire narrative must indicate 'Capital contribution – Panama Private Interest Foundation – Law 25 of 1995.' No central bank exchange-control approval is required. The receiving Panamanian bank will request evidence of the subscriber resolution, source of funds, and beneficial-owner identification, but there is no quantitative ceiling or waiting period for lawful capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements, infrastructure licensing, cloud-service fees, and merchant royalties are cleared through the SWIFT network using standard MT103 for wire transfers and MT700/MT710 for commercial letters of credit where appropriate. For low-value recurring SaaS and app-store-related settlements, MT103 payments to the relevant payment processors and vendors are sufficient. Panamanian banks subject commercial letters of credit to UCP600 rules and the bank's credit-availability relationship. Since Panama's local clearing system is essentially U.S.-dollar based, all domestic payments clear at par; cross-border payments are final in USD and may be routed via correspondent banks in New York or other financial centres.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forwards in USD/EUR, USD/GBP, and USD/JPY with SBP-licensed Panamanian banks where the company demonstrates real commercial exposure from non-USD subscription revenue.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked with international investment-grade counterparties outside Panama for currencies subject to foreign exchange restrictions.
Cross-currency swaps for large multi-currency balances of app-store receivables and operational currency exposure.
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter FX options executed through licensed Panamanian banks or an external broker-dealer permitted by SBP regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax (Impuesto Anual de Fundación) payment certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama; collection through authorized Panamanian banks or DGI online tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 July each calendar year; not tied to foundation registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment is subject to a 10% surcharge plus statutory monthly interest (Panama Tax Code); sustained non-payment for two consecutive years gives the Tax Revenue Directorate grounds to order suspension and eventual strike-off of the Foundation's Public Registry inscription after administrative warning.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent Good-Standing Certification and statutory register audit/inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panama registered agent (corporate/fiduciary service provider) acting under Law 25/1995; not a public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately after the annual tax payment is made and before the agent issues the annual good-standing certificate; renewal cycle must be completed before 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Foundation Council's failure to approve the annual register review is a private governance breach; if the foundation defaults on the annual tax, the agent cannot issue a good-standing certificate, and continued default exposes the foundation to administrative strike-off and agent resignation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and Public Registry Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Beneficial Owner Filing Section, through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the statutory filing window (generally 1 January to 30 June), and additionally within 30 days after any change of beneficiaries, protectors, foundation council members, or founder's reserved rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or to keep the Registry updated prevents issuance of certificates of good standing and constitutes a registrable default; the registered agent may be fined under AML Law 254/2021 and the foundation may be suspended and administratively struck off after the applicable Public Registry pre-cancellation notice period.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a Panama Private Interest Foundation. Law 25/1995 does not establish a turnover, asset, or paid-capital threshold that triggers a mandatory statutory audit. An audit is required only if imposed by the foundation deed, ordered by the Foundation Council with registered-agent approval, requested by a court or Public Registry judge, or if the foundation later becomes a licensed regulated entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The PIF is not subject to a statutory external-audit or financial-statement filing requirement under Panamanian law. Where voluntary financial statements are prepared, IFRS as adopted by the Panama Board of Accountants or the accounting principles expressly designated in the foundation regulations should be used. Because the foundation is taxed on territorial-source income only, records are limited to Panamanian-source activities and administration of local assets.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In each calendar year, before 30 June, the Foundation Council must submit a signed written confirmation to the licensed registered agent listing the current beneficiaries, protector, foundation council members, and any surviving rights reserved by the founder. The registered agent records that confirmation in the statutory register, compares it with previously filed Public Registry records, and files any changes by notarized instrument within 30 days. No annual shareholder meeting is required because a PIF has no share capital.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Statutory Register of Foundation Council Members and Officers
Register of Beneficiaries, Protectors, and Founder's Reserved Rights (UBO file)
Minute/Resolutions Book of the Foundation Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 mandatory; USD 1,500–4,000 per year for a voluntary certified audit
